assertions.claim: every requirement traces to >= 1 case
every case traces to >= 1 requirement
every catalogued case has >= 1 result in a fair run

every requirement has fair non-mutant evidence and the LATEST such result of every instance of every case mapped to it passes; latest = the latest fair run that recorded or PLANNED the instance (older passing runs cannot stand in for a current failure or a planned result that is missing)
every brief fault F1-F13 has a fair result whose observed category equals the recorded prediction (verdict pass; the result's expected category is the catalog's, not one rewritten to match)
each of the 11 outcome categories was observed on the VMs in a fair run
no result is attributed to the device while its preflight was red
no pass verdict carries an attribution

every recorded fault application in a finished run has a verified removal, and every decided (pass/fail) fault-case result of a fair run has a recorded application (no vacuous 'all removed' over missing records)
a result that needed the retry is never verdict pass (a pass only on retry is a FLAKE: fail; with at most one retry, 2 attempts mean attempt 1 did not meet the case)
every run against a mutant build is kind=mutant with its mutant id (so it is never a baseline and never commissions a device)
each of the six brief mutants has >= 1 valid (fair, no infra/runner result) run

every fair run recorded EVERY REQ-10 key (kernel/distro/qdisc/nft for every inventoried VM, python, git_sha, git_dirty, chrony.offset, runs.clean_env, fw_version for every inventoried device) as text in its one valid representation (runner/evidence.check_environment: kernel release, single-line distro, Python version, 40-hex git_sha EQUAL to runs.git_sha, git_dirty/clean_env equal to the run row, a finite SNTP offset with >= 1 sample against witness-ctl inside the preflight clock gate, qdiscs of every lab interface, an nft table, x.y.z firmware); other records of the same facts (runs.kind, mutant, device builds) agree; no key is recorded twice under two spellings. A firmware version may read 'unavailable (<CATEGORY>: ...)' only in a mutant run, for the mutant device, which withheld it. Unfair runs are not evidence and not checked

>= 5 fresh-clone clean baselines (first fair baseline after each distinct golden restore), each COMPLETE (one result per required commissioning instance), all pass, no retry, commissioning every inventoried device
no case verdict/category differs across those runs (nondeterminism would be listed here, not hidden)
no result is pass or attributed to the device when one of its attempts was not a fair device test (outcome runner/infra; for rows before schema v4: unclassifiable or restart observed)

no fair-run capture-flow record marks a flow expected on the wire with 0 packets; and for every CURRENT result (current_evidence: latest fair result per instance, A18's baseline, A14's trials, each mutant's latest valid run) recorded under the capture-flow check, the records are DERIVED from its exchanges (complete and consistent per A24, including 'nothing sent' only for its stated reason) and the case's capture contract (ctl capture always, field capture for fault cases), never trusted and never skipped: every dialled flow x required capture has exactly one record whose expectation matches the exchange facts, and no record is unaccounted for, also on a result whose exchanges are missing. A latest fair result recorded before the check is listed (F3's 5021 flow included)

the latest fair baseline that selected EVERY required commissioning instance (planned it; a run without a plan: executed it), a run with duplicate, conflicting or planned-but-missing results is not skipped, commissions every device of inventory.yaml (catalog-defined prerequisites incl. a valid environment record, runner/db.py commissioning_gaps)

in every fair run each result is a well-formed catalog instance and no case instance has more than one result (pass/fail duplicates, in either order, are ambiguous evidence; rows are kept, never merged)

the bytes behind the current evidence are verified: every evidence file indexed for a current result (and its run's session files) exists with its recorded length and sha256, and every flow it dialled onto the wire is recounted from its hash-verified capture file(s) (runner/evidence.flow_packets, independent of tcpdump): present, and equal to the recorded count. Without an evidence root nothing is verified and this is violated

the reference tables the SQL joins against equal their sources: requirements = docs/requirements.md, cases/kinds and case->requirement map and faults/predictions and mutants = runner/catalog.py, devices = inventory.yaml (a deleted device or case cannot shrink the required sets)

the store is internally consistent: SQLite integrity_check is ok, no row survives its deleted parent (foreign_key_check empty), and the migration record (which says when each obligation starts) agrees with the schema and with the rows each migration governs (acceptance contract I1.1)

every run's status flags agree with its records (environment runs.clean_env, session preflight checks, the runner's recorded contamination cause); every fair run executed exactly its declared selection, one result per planned instance and none unplanned (schema-v5 run plan written before its first case, equal to its indexed plan file; earlier runs: their case evidence directories), with session checks and session evidence indexed; every case evidence directory belongs to a result and every decided result has its directory; with an evidence root, session/environment.json is hash-verified and compared with the environment table and run identity for every recorded session, including mutant and superseded runs (I1.2-I1.7, I10.4)

every current result satisfies its case contract (runner/contract.py): attempt rows 1..n = results.attempts (runner cases 1..2, fault cases 1, gateway/record cases none), summary columns equal their attempts, a pass rests on one attempt with outcome ok and green pre/postflight checks; each attempt's exchanges are ord 1..k in the case's command grammar (a series stops early only at a non-pass or deadline-cut exchange), dial the case's target, are chronological, recompute the attempt category, send nothing only for their stated reason, and a PASS carries its response; required captures and evidence files are indexed; fault applications and measurements as the case records them (I4-I7, I10.2, I10.3)
